text:
Zoe: FYI vendor CapeCloud (Pty) Ltd sent an invoice to Redwood B.V. and are asking us to gross-up for a 10% South African withholding tax. They charged no VAT. Any quick guidance? :wave:

Miguel: Do not pay until we verify. Who's the invoiced Redwood entity? That determines VAT vs withholding.

Zoe: Invoice shows payee: Redwood B.V. (Netherlands). Invoice snippet: ```
Invoice #: 2026-04-01-CC
Supplier: CapeCloud (Pty) Ltd
Reg no: 2019/123456/07
Amount: EUR 12,000
Description: Managed security monitoring (monthly)
Vendor note: "Please gross up 10% to cover South African withholding tax so supplier receives net."
```

Priya: Quick tax note: South Africa can withhold on certain payments to non-residents (e.g., royalties, some technical services) but it's specific. For services billed to a non-resident EU entity, SA WHT isn't automatic — vendor needs to show legal basis. Also VAT is separate; if invoiced to Redwood B.V., EU import VAT/reverse-charge rules may apply on your side, not SA VAT.

Priya: Our policy is not to gross-up unless contractually obligated or there's an official tax ruling. Ask vendor to provide: (1) official SA tax determination or certificate showing WHT applies, (2) tax residency certificate, (3) calculation showing how 10% was derived, and (4) the contract clause if they claim commercial gross-up.

Alex: Also ask them to reissue invoice clarifying VAT treatment and the invoiced legal entity (billing to Redwood B.V. is important). If they instead want us to withhold, they should tell us the withholding account details and paperwork needed for them to claim credit in RSA.

Zoe: I'll email them. Draft reply: "We cannot gross-up by default. Please provide a South African tax authority notice or legal basis for the 10% withholding, a tax residency certificate, and reissue the invoice clarifying VAT/tax treatment and the invoiced Redwood entity. Payment is on hold until validated. If you are requesting we withhold, please supply the documentation we need to remit and any treaty reference"

Miguel: I've set HOLD in AP. invoice-bot, confirm.

invoice-bot: Payment status updated: HOLD for invoice 2026-04-01-CC set by Miguel  reason: awaiting vendor tax docs.

Zoe: Tagging Legal/TAX if they push back. Legal, please flag if contract mentions gross-up or if we should propose commercial alternative (e.g., net invoice + vendor provides local certificate to reclaim).

Legal: Will review contract if vendor produces it. If vendor insists and it's not contractually required, we treat as commercial negotiation, not a tax obligation. Also confirm which Redwood legal entity actually received the services (operational place of supply can matter).

Priya: If vendor cites treaty relief or a specific SA Income Tax Act provision, ask them to quote the article and provide the formal notice/case. Without that, we hold payment and do not gross-up.

Zoe: Thanks team 44d I'll send now and paste vendor reply in thread.
